course: Core Pure 2 (PMT topic sheets, owner folder Year 2)
cropMethod: Scheme regions run from each "Qn." label to the next label (labels tightened to their own text line); every content box on every scheme page is assigned to exactly one question (asserted). Crops are split only at blank rows or table rules so no crop is taller than it is wide, and each cut leaves at least 20 pt. Figures are 200 dpi crops including their printed captions.

rubric.easy: Routine: a standard result or procedure applied directly, in short structured parts; no insight or choice of method needed.
rubric.medium: Standard methods combined over several steps, or one signposted non-routine step; moderate algebra; guided modelling.
rubric.difficult: Problem-solving: unstructured or multi-concept, the method must be chosen without guidance, or long and delicate algebra, geometry or extended modelling. (The brief calls this level "hard"; Luisa stores it as "difficult".)

resolutions.why: Every part names its method (use part (a), de Moivre); one signposted non-routine step plus a 2-mark reason. Same rule as v0.75: long but fully signposted work is medium.
Multi-concept (summation formulae plus tan periodicity) and part (c) sets up and solves a cubic, rejecting a root, for 6 marks; kept.
Standard method of differences in three short signposted parts, 7 marks.

rerate.finalAgreement: 9/10 (0.9): the reviewer rating was adopted for ch1/q4 (medium) and ch2/q9 (easy) by the rubric; for ch2/q2 the rubric supports the import rating (difficult).

mathsReview: An independent agent compared all 61 rendered app questions with the rendered source pages (zooming into maths where needed): 0 discrepancies in wording, numbers, signs, exponents, part labels or marks; both source slips below are real and no other slip was repaired. All 12 figures are whole with captions as printed. Its scheme sample (12 questions over all 8 chapters, including all three sampled totals-only questions) found every scheme complete with nothing from another question; every sheet's scheme pages are contiguous to its last page, so Year 2 has no appendix or misplaced block (also confirmed by an OCR scan of every scheme page). It compared all 61 against 578 bank questions and found no missed duplicates.

sourceNotes.note: Source slip kept as printed: the sheet prints "r(cosθ θ+ isinθ)" for the form r(cos θ + i sin θ), exactly as in the Core Pure 1 copy of this question.
Source slip kept as printed: part (c) reads "in the form p + 1/6 ln q, p and q are constants"; the original 9FM0/01 Sample paper has "where p and q are constants". The maths is unaffected.

notDuplicates.why: Different equation (64cosh^4 x - 64cosh^2 x - 9 = 0 against sinh 2x = 3 sinh x); only the boilerplate instruction lines are shared.

duplicateRule: The copy keeps a duplicateOf link and neither copy is deleted. A generated exam paper or booklet drops the copy whenever its original is in the pool; a hand-picked selection containing both shows a note.
partMarks: Ch.2 Q4, Ch.3 Q2, Ch.5 Q5, Ch.6 Q3 and Ch.6 Q6 print only the question total; no part marks were added.
coreOneCopiesUpdated: In this release the six Core Pure 1 copies whose originals cover several Core Pure 1 chapters gained those chapter keys (ch2/q9, ch6/q7, ch7/q3, ch8/q5, ch8/q8, ch8/q9), following the v0.75 review.
printInspection: Real Chrome PDFs inspected page by page: a Core Pure 2 practice paper (figures, long display equations) one per page and condensed with solutions on and off, and a mixed past-paper + Core Pure 1 + Core Pure 2 exam paper (no source on question pages; exact source and ID in the scheme). No warnings and no element wider than its page.
